channel.title: North Wales Pioneer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from North Wales Pioneer (northwalespioneer.co.uk)

item.title: Colwyn Bay private school to open sixth form boarding house from next year
item.description: A private school in Colwyn Bay will welcome sixth form students into a new boarding house for the next academic year.

item.title: North Wales coast trains face cancellation as heavy rain 'disrupts' services
item.description: Train services on the North Wales Coast Line may see cancellations after heavy rain flooded a stretch of the railway line.

item.title: 'Exceptional' Llandudno seafront hotel goes on the market for six-figure sum
item.description: A seafront hotel in Llandudno which performs "exceptionally well" has gone on the market for more than half a million pounds.

item.title: Road in Conwy county closed due to flooding as Storm Bram batters region
item.description: A road in Conwy has closed due to flooding.

item.title: Conwy main road closed due to fallen tree - people told to 'avoid area'
item.description: A main road in Conwy has closed because of a fallen tree.

item.title: Crackdown on North Wales trains to ensure safe journeys during Christmas
item.description: Transport for Wales and British Transport Police are increasing patrols across the rail network this December as operations return to improve safety.

item.title: Betsi under fire for removing sandwiches from North Wales emergency department
item.description: Ysbyty Glan Clwyd has now stopped providing sandwiches in the emergency department, despite some patients being left for hours in corridors before they are seen.

item.title: Conwy Council moves to finally unlock Porth Eirias potential with wider retail scope
item.description: Conwy County Council is seeking planning permission to widen its uses of Porth Eirias and cancel retail restrictions governing what can be sold at the building’s empty units.

item.title: Developer vows Colwyn Bay Civic Centre revival within two years
item.description: Robert Roberts of Eirias Coastal Park Hotel Ltd said: “We are converting the civic centre into a 53-bed apart hotel with 50 electric vehicle charging points with a 24-hour vending shop. At the moment, we are trying to get the infrastructure in place. This should be completed within two years.”

item.title: Road in Llandudno town centre to be closed for some time after collision
item.description: Police are urging people to stay away from a road in Llandudno town centre.
